case.title: Distinguish chance from certainty — analyze
case.topic: Analyzing variation in a specified random simulation

messages.content: A simulation independently samples 20 observations from the same fixed random model on each run. Some run means differ. A report calls any such difference proof that the model changed. Analyze that reasoning.
All runs use the same sampling model.
Which part of your account are you least certain about?
Different run means cannot occur under a fixed model, so any difference proves a change in the model.

understands: Recognizes the stated common sampling model across runs: “All runs use the same sampling model.” This establishes recognition of a premise, not understanding of its implications for sample means.
potentialMisconceptions: The claim “Different run means cannot occur under a fixed model, so any difference proves a change in the model.” supports the hypothesis that the learner conflates a fixed sampling distribution with identical realized sample means, treating ordinary sampling variation as conclusive evidence of model change.
missingConcepts: The response does not demonstrate understanding that independent samples of 20 observations from a fixed, nondegenerate model can produce different sample means.
The response does not distinguish variation in a sample statistic from a change in the underlying model, or analyze why differing means alone do not establish such a change.
uncertainty: There is no explanation of the learner’s reasoning beyond the asserted impossibility, so the precise source of the misconception is uncertain.

The transcript provides no evidence about the learner’s understanding of independence or the effect of sample size; lack of evidence on these points should not be treated as an additional incorrect belief.

strategy.title: Distinguish chance from certainty
strategy.objective: Separate possible outcomes, expected patterns, and variability under a specified probabilistic process.
strategy.useWhen: The student treats an expected proportion as an exact outcome or interprets variation as proof that the process is not random.
requirements: A defined random process and trial conditions
avoidWhen: The target concerns only aggregate versus individual properties
constructionRules: Specify the process and what is repeated or sampled.
Ask about one distinction between expectation, possibility, and realized outcomes.
Do not assume independence or equate randomness with equal probabilities.
interpretationRules: A single unlikely outcome need not refute a model.
Separate model misspecification from ordinary sampling variability.
Treat response patterns as tentative evidence; ambiguous, unsupported, or prerequisite-confounded answers remain unresolved.

enum: Analyzes whether differing run means alone establish a changed model under the stated fixed independent sampling process.

response.rationale: The active Analyze task concerns an unsupported inference from differing sample means to model change. The random sampling process, sample size, and independence are specified, so this strategy can probe the distinction between a fixed model and realized outcomes without adding a new task.

plan.targetQuote: Different run means cannot occur under a fixed model, so any difference proves a change in the model.
plan.rubricItem: Analyzes whether differing run means alone establish a changed model under the stated fixed independent sampling process.
plan.objective: Probe the learner's reasoning about whether fixing the sampling model forces independent samples of 20 observations to have identical means, and hence whether a difference alone proves model change.
plan.scenario: The simulation independently samples 20 observations from the same fixed random model on each run. Some run means differ, and the report treats any difference as proof that the model changed.
assumptions: Each run samples 20 observations from the stated fixed random model.
Sampling is independent as specified in the original task.
Some observed run means differ; no particular distribution, parameter values, or numerical means are supplied.
heldFixed: The sample size of 20 per run
varied: The observations obtained on separate runs
plan.construction: Ask: "You said different run means cannot occur under a fixed model. In this simulation, each run independently samples 20 observations from the same model. Why would keeping the model fixed require the run means to be identical? Use how the observations are sampled to explain your reasoning." Keep this as one probe of the asserted necessity, without supplying the resolution or asking for a calculation.
plan.prerequisitesSatisfied: The transcript supplies a defined random process, sample size, independent sampling, observed differences, and the learner's explicit inference. No probability calculation or additional distributional information is needed to probe that inference.
limitations: A fixed model's specific distribution is not supplied; do not invent numerical probabilities or assumptions about its form.
The learner's understanding of independence and sample size is not established; an unclear response may reflect prerequisite uncertainty rather than a uniquely identified misconception.
A correct conclusion without reasoning does not demonstrate analysis of the inference.

responseSignals.hypothesis: The learner conflates a fixed generating model with fixed realized outcomes.
responseSignals.responsePattern: Argues that the same model must produce the same observations or mean on every run, using sameness of the model as the justification.
responseSignals.interpretation: Supports the targeted conflation, although further evidence might be needed to distinguish beliefs about random sampling from beliefs about simulation implementation.

responseSignals.hypothesis: The learner can distinguish a fixed model from variable sample outcomes.
responseSignals.responsePattern: Explains that separate random samples can contain different observations and therefore yield different means even when the sampling model is unchanged, connecting this to why the difference alone is not proof.
responseSignals.interpretation: Supports understanding of the targeted relationship and analysis of the report's inference.

responseSignals.responsePattern: Retracts the claim or says that means can differ, but supplies no account of the sampled observations or instead assumes an unspecified implementation detail.
responseSignals.interpretation: The conclusion alone is insufficient evidence of understanding; the intended relationship remains ambiguous.

messages.content: Begin the learning-by-teaching session for the supplied curriculum.

A simulation independently samples 20 observations from the same fixed random model on each run. Some run means differ. A report calls any such difference proof that the model changed. Analyze that reasoning.
All runs use the same sampling model.
Which part of your account are you least certain about?
Different run means cannot occur under a fixed model, so any difference proves a change in the model.
